source.text: וּֽלְנָעֳמִ֞י מוֹדַ֣ע לְאִישָׁ֗הּ אִ֚ישׁ גִּבּ֣וֹר חַ֔יִל מִמִּשְׁפַּ֖חַת אֱלִימֶ֑לֶךְ וּשְׁמ֖וֹ בֹּֽעַז׃

records.literal_gloss: And to Naomi [was] a relative of her husband, a man mighty of wealth, from [the] clan of Elimelech, and his name [was] Boaz.

en.L: Now Naomi had a relative of her husband, a man mighty in wealth, from the clan of Elimelech, and his name [was] Boaz.
en.B: Naomi had a relative on her husband's side, a man of wealth and standing from the clan of Elimelech. His name was Boaz.
en.R: Naomi had a relative on her husband's side named Boaz. He was a rich and respected man from Elimelech's clan.

sw.L: Naye Naomi alikuwa na jamaa wa mumewe, mtu hodari wa mali, wa ukoo wa Elimeleki, na jina lake [lilikuwa] Boazi.
sw.B: Naomi alikuwa na jamaa wa upande wa mumewe, mtu mwenye mali na heshima, wa ukoo wa Elimeleki. Jina lake lilikuwa Boazi.
sw.R: Naomi alikuwa na jamaa wa upande wa mumewe aitwaye Boazi. Alikuwa mtu tajiri na mwenye heshima wa ukoo wa Elimeleki.

es.L: Y Noemí tenía un pariente de su marido, un hombre poderoso en riqueza, del clan de Elimelec, y su nombre [era] Booz.
es.B: Noemí tenía un pariente por parte de su marido, un hombre rico e influyente del clan de Elimelec. Se llamaba Booz.
es.R: Noemí tenía un pariente por parte de su esposo que se llamaba Booz. Era un hombre rico y respetado del clan de Elimelec.

decisions.choice: a man mighty in wealth: a man of substance and good name
decisions.reason: The phrase can describe a strong warrior (Judges 6:12; 11:1), but here, in a story of fields and harvest, it means a man of wealth, ability and standing in his town. The same word chayil is used of Ruth in 3:11, "a woman of worth", so the two are matched before they meet.

decisions.choice: relative: one known to the family, a kinsman
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text and the reading tradition give two slightly different forms of this word here, but both name a man close to the family: a relative or one known as kin. A word from the same root names Boaz as "our relative" in 3:2. Verse 20 shows how close he is.

decisions.choice: the narrator tells the reader first
decisions.reason: The verse interrupts the story to introduce Boaz before Ruth meets him. The reader knows who owns the field in verse 3; Ruth and Naomi do not learn it until verse 19.

decisions.choice: a man of wealth and standing (Balanced); a rich and respected man (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give both sides of the phrase, his wealth and his good name. Literal keeps "mighty in wealth".

source.text: וַתֹּאמֶר֩ ר֨וּת הַמּוֹאֲבִיָּ֜ה אֶֽל־נָעֳמִ֗י אֵֽלְכָה־נָּ֤א הַשָּׂדֶה֙ וַאֲלַקֳטָּ֣הבַשִׁבֳּלִ֔יםאַחַ֕ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֶמְצָא־חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינָ֑יו וַתֹּ֥אמֶר לָ֖הּ לְכִ֥י בִתִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Ruth the Moabite to Naomi, let me go, please, [to] the field and let me glean among the ears behind [one] who I find favor in his eyes. And she said to her, go, my daughter.

en.L: And Ruth the Moabite said to Naomi, "Please let me go to the field and glean among the ears of grain behind [someone] in whose eyes I find favor." And she said to her, "Go, my daughter."
en.B: Ruth the Moabite said to Naomi, "Let me go out to the fields and glean ears of grain behind anyone who will look on me with favor." Naomi answered her, "Go, my daughter."
en.R: Ruth, the woman from Moab, said to Naomi, "Let me go out to the fields. I will pick up the grain the harvesters leave behind, if someone will be kind enough to let me." Naomi said to her, "Go ahead, my daughter."

sw.L: Naye Ruthu Mmoabu akamwambia Naomi, "Tafadhali niache niende shambani niokote masazo kati ya masuke nyuma ya [mtu] ambaye nitapata kibali machoni pake." Naye akamwambia, "Nenda, binti yangu."
sw.B: Ruthu Mmoabu alimwambia Naomi, "Niache niende mashambani niokote masazo ya masuke nyuma ya yeyote atakayenitazama kwa kibali." Naomi akamjibu, "Nenda, binti yangu."
sw.R: Ruthu, yule mwanamke wa Moabu, alimwambia Naomi, "Niache niende mashambani. Nitaokota nafaka ambayo wavunaji wanaiacha nyuma, kama kuna mtu atakayekuwa mwema kiasi cha kuniruhusu." Naomi alimwambia, "Haya nenda, binti yangu."

es.L: Y Rut la moabita dijo a Noemí: «Déjame ir, te ruego, al campo, y recogeré espigas detrás de [aquel] a cuyos ojos halle gracia». Y ella le dijo: «Ve, hija mía».
es.B: Rut la moabita le dijo a Noemí: «Déjame ir a los campos a recoger espigas detrás de quien me mire con favor». Noemí le respondió: «Ve, hija mía».
es.R: Rut, la mujer de Moab, le dijo a Noemí: «Déjame ir a los campos. Recogeré el grano que dejan atrás los segadores, si alguien es tan amable de permitírmelo». Noemí le dijo: «Anda, hija mía».

decisions.choice: glean: gather the grain the harvesters left behind
decisions.reason: God's law told landowners not to reap to the very edges of a field or go back for what was dropped or forgotten, but to leave it for the poor, the sojourner, the fatherless and the widow (Leviticus 19:9-10; 23:22; Deuteronomy 24:19). Ruth is poor, foreign and widowed, so she has a right to glean.

decisions.choice: find favor in his eyes: be treated kindly
decisions.reason: To find favor in someone's eyes is to win his goodwill. Even with the law on her side, Ruth hopes to find a landowner or reaper who will let her glean and treat her well; the same phrase comes back in verses 10 and 13.

decisions.choice: Ruth the Moabite: her foreign origin kept in view
decisions.reason: The narrator keeps calling her "the Moabite" (1:22; 2:21) and others do too (verse 6). The story never lets the reader forget that a foreign woman is the one who shows such loyalty.

decisions.choice: pick up the grain the harvesters leave behind, if someone will be kind enough to let me
decisions.reason: Readable explains what gleaning is and says what "finding favor" means here: someone letting her glean.

decisions.choice: "kuokota masazo" (to pick up what is left) for gleaning; Readable "kuokota nafaka ambayo wavunaji wanaiacha nyuma"
decisions.reason: Swahili has no single verb for gleaning; "masazo" are the leftovers, and Readable spells out the custom (m1), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Naomi calls Ruth "binti yangu" (my daughter); Ruth speaks to her with the singular "wewe"
decisions.reason: As Ruth 1, the affectionate word of an older woman to a younger; Boaz uses the same words to Ruth in verse 8 (m2 there).

decisions.choice: "recoger espigas"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb means gathering the grain the harvesters left behind (m1); "recoger espigas" is the Spanish phrase for it, and Readable explains it, as the English Readable does.

source.text: וַתֵּ֤לֶךְ וַתָּבוֹא֙ וַתְּלַקֵּ֣ט בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה אַחֲרֵ֖י הַקֹּצְרִ֑ים וַיִּ֣קֶר מִקְרֶ֔הָ חֶלְקַ֤ת הַשָּׂדֶה֙ לְבֹ֔עַז אֲשֶׁ֖ר מִמִּשְׁפַּ֥חַת אֱלִימֶֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And she went and came and gleaned in the field behind the harvesters; and chanced her chance [on the] portion of the field belonging to Boaz, who [was] from [the] clan of Elimelech.

en.L: So she went and came and gleaned in the field behind the harvesters, and her chance chanced upon the portion of the field belonging to Boaz, who [was] from the clan of Elimelech.
en.B: So she set out, came to a field and gleaned behind the harvesters. As it happened, she came to the part of the field that belonged to Boaz, who was from the clan of Elimelech.
en.R: So Ruth went out and began picking up grain behind the harvesters. It just so happened that she was working in a field that belonged to Boaz, the man from Elimelech's clan.

sw.L: Naye akaenda, akafika, akaokota masazo shambani nyuma ya wavunaji; na bahati yake ikamwangukia sehemu ya shamba iliyokuwa ya Boazi, aliyekuwa wa ukoo wa Elimeleki.
sw.B: Basi aliondoka, akafika shambani, akaokota masazo nyuma ya wavunaji. Ikatukia kwamba alifika katika sehemu ya shamba iliyokuwa ya Boazi, aliyekuwa wa ukoo wa Elimeleki.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Ruthu alikwenda, akaanza kuokota nafaka nyuma ya wavunaji. Ikatukia tu kwamba alikuwa akifanya kazi katika shamba lililokuwa la Boazi, yule mtu wa ukoo wa Elimeleki.

es.L: Y fue, y llegó y recogió espigas en el campo detrás de los segadores; y quiso su suerte que [diera con] la parcela del campo que pertenecía a Booz, que [era] del clan de Elimelec.
es.B: Así que salió, llegó a un campo y se puso a recoger espigas detrás de los segadores. Y dio la casualidad de que llegó a la parte del campo que pertenecía a Booz, que era del clan de Elimelec.
es.R: Así que Rut salió y comenzó a recoger grano detrás de los segadores. Y resultó que estaba trabajando en un campo que pertenecía a Booz, el hombre del clan de Elimelec.

decisions.choice: her chance chanced: it happened, as far as she knew, by chance
decisions.reason: The verb and its noun come from the same root, a doubled way of saying it just happened. From Ruth's point of view it was luck. The narrator, who has already introduced Boaz (verse 1), lets the reader see more: Naomi will praise the LORD for it in verse 20.

decisions.choice: the portion of the field: one family's plot
decisions.reason: The farmland around a town was one open stretch divided into family plots without fences. A gleaner could move from one owner's strip to another without knowing whose land she was on.

decisions.choice: as it happened (Balanced); it just so happened (Readable)
decisions.reason: Both keep the sense of chance in plain words; Literal keeps the doubled Hebrew "her chance chanced".

source.text: וְהִנֵּה־בֹ֗עַז בָּ֚א מִבֵּ֣ית לֶ֔חֶם וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לַקּוֹצְרִ֖ים יְהוָ֣ה עִמָּכֶ֑ם וַיֹּ֥אמְרוּ ל֖וֹ יְבָרֶכְךָ֥ יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And look, Boaz [was] coming from Bethlehem and said to the harvesters, Yahweh [be] with you. And they said to him, may bless you Yahweh.

en.L: And look, Boaz came from Bethlehem and said to the harvesters, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} [be] with you!" And they said to him, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless you!"
en.B: Just then Boaz arrived from Bethlehem. He greeted the harvesters, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} be with you!" and they answered him, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless you!"
en.R: Just then Boaz came out from Bethlehem. He said to the harvesters, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be with you!" They answered, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless you!"

sw.L: Na tazama, Boazi akaja kutoka Bethlehemu, akawaambia wavunaji, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [na awe] pamoja nanyi!" Nao wakamwambia, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na akubariki!"
sw.B: Wakati huo huo Boazi alifika kutoka Bethlehemu. Aliwasalimu wavunaji, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} awe pamoja nanyi!" Nao wakamjibu, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akubariki!"
sw.R: Wakati huo huo Boazi alitoka Bethlehemu. Aliwaambia wavunaji, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} awe pamoja nanyi!" Nao wakajibu, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akubariki!"

es.L: Y he aquí, Booz vino de Belén y dijo a los segadores: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} [sea] con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}». Y ellos le dijeron: «Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te bendiga».
es.B: En ese momento llegó Booz de Belén. Saludó a los segadores: «¡{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} sea con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}!». Y ellos le respondieron: «¡Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te bendiga!».
es.R: En ese momento llegó Booz de Belén. Les dijo a los segadores: «¡Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} esté con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}!». Ellos le respondieron: «¡Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te bendiga!».

decisions.choice: and look: Boaz arrives at that very moment
decisions.reason: The word hinneh draws attention to what happens next, as if the reader were watching. Ruth has only just come to the field when its owner appears.

decisions.choice: greeting and reply as blessings
decisions.reason: People greeted one another with a blessing in the LORD's name (Judges 6:12; Psalm 129:8). The exchange shows a landowner and workers on good terms, and a man who speaks of God in everyday life.

decisions.choice: just then
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable express hinneh by its timing; Literal keeps "look".

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר בֹּ֨עַז֙ לְנַעֲר֔וֹ הַנִּצָּ֖ב עַל־הַקּֽוֹצְרִ֑ים לְמִ֖י הַנַּעֲרָ֥ה הַזֹּֽאת׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Boaz to his young man, the [one] stationed over the harvesters, to whom [is] this young woman?

en.L: And Boaz said to his young man who was set over the harvesters, "To whom [does] this young woman [belong]?"
en.B: Boaz asked his servant who was in charge of the harvesters, "Whose young woman is this?"
en.R: Boaz asked the man in charge of his harvesters, "Who is that young woman? What family is she from?"

sw.L: Naye Boazi akamwambia kijana wake aliyesimamia wavunaji, "Msichana huyu ni wa nani?"
sw.B: Boazi alimwuliza mtumishi wake aliyekuwa msimamizi wa wavunaji, "Msichana huyu ni wa nani?"
sw.R: Boazi alimwuliza mtu aliyekuwa msimamizi wa wavunaji wake, "Msichana yule ni nani? Ni wa jamaa gani?"

es.L: Y Booz dijo a su muchacho, el que estaba puesto sobre los segadores: «¿De quién [es] esta joven?».
es.B: Booz le preguntó al criado que estaba a cargo de los segadores: «¿De quién es esta joven?».
es.R: Booz le preguntó al hombre que estaba a cargo de sus segadores: «¿Quién es esa joven? ¿De qué familia es?».

decisions.choice: his young man set over the harvesters: his foreman
decisions.reason: Na'ar means a young man, and often a young man in someone's service, a worker or attendant. This one has been put in charge of the reapers.

decisions.choice: to whom does she belong?: what household is she part of
decisions.reason: A woman was known by the household she belonged to: her father's, her husband's, or a master's. Boaz asks not her name but her family and place, and the answer in verse 6 tells him exactly that.

decisions.choice: young woman: na'arah
decisions.reason: The word is used of a girl or young woman, often unmarried and sometimes in service. Ruth is a widow but still young; Boaz is older (3:10).

decisions.choice: servant (Balanced); the man in charge (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "young man", the word's basic sense; Balanced and Readable say what he was to Boaz.

decisions.choice: What family is she from?
decisions.reason: Readable adds the second question to show what "whose" means here.

source.text: וַיַּ֗עַן הַנַּ֛עַר הַנִּצָּ֥ב עַל־הַקּוֹצְרִ֖ים וַיֹּאמַ֑ר נַעֲרָ֤ה מֽוֹאֲבִיָּה֙ הִ֔יא הַשָּׁ֥בָה עִֽם־נָעֳמִ֖י מִשְּׂדֵ֥ה מוֹאָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered the young man, the [one] stationed over the harvesters, and said, a young woman, a Moabite, [is] she, the [one who] returned with Naomi from [the] field of Moab.

en.L: And the young man who was set over the harvesters answered and said, "She [is] a young Moabite woman, the [one] who returned with Naomi from the country of Moab.
en.B: The servant in charge of the harvesters answered, "She is a young Moabite woman, the one who came back with Naomi from the country of Moab.
en.R: The man answered, "She is the young woman from Moab who came back with Naomi.

sw.L: Naye yule kijana aliyesimamia wavunaji akajibu, akasema, "Yeye [ni] msichana Mmoabu, yule aliyerudi pamoja na Naomi kutoka nchi ya Moabu.
sw.B: Mtumishi aliyekuwa msimamizi wa wavunaji alijibu, "Yeye ni msichana Mmoabu, yule aliyerudi pamoja na Naomi kutoka nchi ya Moabu.
sw.R: Yule mtu alijibu, "Yeye ni yule msichana wa Moabu aliyerudi pamoja na Naomi.

es.L: Y el muchacho que estaba puesto sobre los segadores respondió y dijo: «Es una joven moabita, la que volvió con Noemí de los campos de Moab.
es.B: El criado encargado de los segadores le respondió: «Es una joven moabita, la que volvió con Noemí de la región de Moab.
es.R: El hombre le contestó: «Es la joven de Moab que vino con Noemí.

decisions.choice: returned: came back with Naomi
decisions.reason: Ruth had never lived in Bethlehem, yet the same verb is used of her as of Naomi (1:22). By joining Naomi's people (1:16) she has, in a sense, come home with her.

decisions.choice: a young Moabite woman: her origin first
decisions.reason: The foreman's first words are that she is a Moabite. Moab and Israel had a hard history (Numbers 22-25; Deuteronomy 23:4-5), so this is the first thing people notice about her.

decisions.choice: the field of Moab: the country of Moab
decisions.reason: The word for field also means open country or territory, as in 1:1 and 1:6.

decisions.choice: from Moab ... came back with Naomi
decisions.reason: Readable says "from Moab" once, so the country is not named twice in one short sentence.

source.text: וַתֹּ֗אמֶר אֲלַקֳטָה־נָּא֙ וְאָסַפְתִּ֣י בָֽעֳמָרִ֔ים אַחֲרֵ֖י הַקּוֹצְרִ֑ים וַתָּב֣וֹא וַֽתַּעֲמ֗וֹד מֵאָ֤ז הַבֹּ֨קֶר֙ וְעַד־עַ֔תָּה זֶ֛ה שִׁבְתָּ֥הּ הַבַּ֖יִת מְעָֽט׃

records.literal_gloss: And she said, let me glean, please, and I will gather among the sheaves behind the harvesters. And she came and has stood from then, the morning, and until now; this her sitting [in] the house [is a] little.

en.L: And she said, 'Please let me glean and gather among the sheaves behind the harvesters.' So she came and has stood from the morning until now; her sitting in the house [has been] little."
en.B: She said, 'Please let me glean and gather among the sheaves behind the harvesters.' So she came, and she has been on her feet from early morning until now, except for a short rest in the shelter."
en.R: She asked me, 'Please let me pick up grain among the bundles behind the harvesters.' She came early this morning, and she has been working ever since. She has only stopped for a little while to rest in the shelter."

sw.L: Naye alisema, 'Tafadhali niache niokote masazo na kukusanya kati ya miganda nyuma ya wavunaji.' Basi akaja, akasimama tangu asubuhi mpaka sasa; kukaa kwake nyumbani [kumekuwa] kidogo."
sw.B: Alisema, 'Tafadhali niache niokote masazo na kukusanya kati ya miganda nyuma ya wavunaji.' Kwa hiyo alikuja, naye amekuwa kazini tangu asubuhi na mapema mpaka sasa, ila tu alipumzika kidogo kibandani."
sw.R: Aliniomba, 'Tafadhali niache niokote nafaka kati ya mafungu nyuma ya wavunaji.' Alikuja asubuhi na mapema, naye amekuwa akifanya kazi tangu wakati huo. Amesimama tu kwa muda mfupi kupumzika kibandani."

es.L: Y dijo: “Déjame recoger espigas, te ruego, y juntar entre las gavillas detrás de los segadores”. Y vino y ha estado en pie desde la mañana hasta ahora; su descanso en la casa [ha sido] poco».
es.B: Me dijo: “Por favor, déjame recoger espigas y juntarlas entre las gavillas detrás de los segadores”. Así que vino, y ha estado de pie desde la mañana hasta ahora, salvo un breve descanso en el cobertizo».
es.R: Me pidió: “Por favor, déjame recoger grano entre los manojos, detrás de los segadores”. Vino temprano esta mañana y ha estado trabajando desde entonces. Solo se ha detenido un ratito para descansar en el cobertizo».

decisions.choice: her sitting in the house has been little: she has hardly rested
alternatives: she has stood waiting since morning
she has not rested even a little
decisions.reason: The end of the verse is very hard in the Hebrew, word for word "this her sitting the house little". The likeliest sense is that she has kept working since morning and rested only briefly in the field shelter. Others take it to mean that she has stood waiting for permission since morning, or read it as "she has not rested in the field even a little", as the ancient Greek translation does. The wording may have been damaged in copying.

decisions.choice: gather among the sheaves: glean where the cut grain lies bundled
decisions.reason: Gleaners usually followed behind once the sheaves had been tied and taken away. Ruth asks to gather among the sheaves themselves, more than the law granted, and in verse 15 Boaz allows it. The words may also mean that she asked to gather her gleanings into bundles.

decisions.choice: the house: the field shelter
decisions.reason: In the middle of a field "the house" is most likely a simple shelter where workers rested out of the sun.

decisions.choice: on her feet ... (Balanced); working ever since (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Stood" here means she has stayed at work; Balanced and Readable say so. Literal keeps "stood".

decisions.choice: She asked me
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the foreman is reporting Ruth's own request to him.

source.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ בֹּ֨עַז אֶל־ר֜וּת הֲל֧וֹא שָׁמַ֣עַתְּ בִּתִּ֗י אַל־תֵּלְכִי֙ לִלְקֹט֙ בְּשָׂדֶ֣ה אַחֵ֔ר וְגַ֛ם לֹ֥א תַעֲבוּרִ֖י מִזֶּ֑ה וְכֹ֥ה תִדְבָּקִ֖ין עִם־נַעֲרֹתָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Boaz to Ruth, [have] you not heard, my daughter? Do not go to glean in another field, and also do not pass on from this, and thus stay close with my young women.

en.L: And Boaz said to Ruth, "Have you not heard, my daughter? Do not go to glean in another field, and also do not pass on from this [one], but keep close here to my young women.
en.B: Then Boaz said to Ruth, "Listen to me, my daughter. Do not go to glean in any other field, and do not move on from this one. Stay here close to my young women.
en.R: Boaz said to Ruth, "Listen to me, my daughter. Do not go off to pick up grain in any other field. Do not leave this one. Stay here with the young women who work for me.

sw.L: Naye Boazi akamwambia Ruthu, "Je, hujasikia, binti yangu? Usiende kuokota masazo katika shamba lingine, wala usiondoke hapa, bali ukae karibu na wasichana wangu hapa.

decisions.choice: have you not heard?: listen to me
decisions.reason: The question is a polite way of asking for attention: "listen carefully".

decisions.choice: my daughter: an older man speaking kindly
decisions.reason: Naomi calls Ruth "my daughter" (verse 2), and Boaz does the same. It is a warm address from an older person to a younger one, and suggests that Boaz is older than Ruth (3:10).

decisions.choice: keep close: stay with, cling to
decisions.reason: The verb dabaq is the one used of Ruth clinging to Naomi (1:14). Boaz asks her to keep close to his young women, and she does (verse 23).

decisions.choice: Listen to me (Balanced); Listen (Readable)
decisions.reason: The question "have you not heard?" is given its sense; Literal keeps the question.

decisions.choice: "hija mía" for Boaz to Ruth; "tú" between Boaz and Ruth, and "mi señor" from Ruth (verse 13)
decisions.reason: Boaz speaks to Ruth as an older man speaking kindly (m2), and "hija mía" says that in Spanish too. As everywhere in this translation, one person is addressed with "tú"; Ruth's respect for Boaz is carried by "mi señor" and by her humble words, not by "usted".

source.text: עֵינַ֜יִךְ בַּשָּׂדֶ֤ה אֲשֶׁר־יִקְצֹרוּן֙ וְהָלַ֣כְתִּאַחֲרֵיהֶ֔ן הֲל֥וֹא צִוִּ֛יתִי אֶת־הַנְּעָרִ֖ים לְבִלְתִּ֣י נָגְעֵ֑ךְ וְצָמִ֗ת וְהָלַכְתְּ֙ אֶל־הַכֵּלִ֔ים וְשָׁתִ֕ית מֵאֲשֶׁ֥ר יִשְׁאֲב֖וּן הַנְּעָרִֽים׃

sw.L: Macho yako [na yawe] juu ya shamba wanalovuna, uwafuate. Je, sikuwaamuru vijana wasikuguse? Nawe ukiona kiu, nenda kwenye vyombo unywe katika yale wanayoteka vijana."
sw.B: Yaangalie shamba wanalovuna, uwafuate wale wanawake. Nimewaamuru vijana wasikuguse. Nawe ukiona kiu, nenda kwenye mitungi unywe maji yaliyotekwa na vijana."
sw.R: Angalia ni shamba gani wanalofanyia kazi, uwafuate wanawake huko. Nimewaambia vijana wasikusumbue. Ukiona kiu, nenda ukanywe maji kutoka kwenye mitungi ambayo vijana wameijaza."

es.L: [Estén] tus ojos en el campo que sieguen, y ve tras ellas. ¿No he mandado a los criados que no te toquen? Y cuando tengas sed, ve a las vasijas y bebe de lo que sacan los criados».
es.B: Fíjate en el campo que están segando y sigue a las mujeres. He ordenado a los criados que no te pongan la mano encima. Y cuando tengas sed, ve a los cántaros y bebe del agua que han sacado los criados».
es.R: Fíjate en qué campo están trabajando, y sigue allí a las mujeres. Les he dicho a los muchachos que no te molesten. Cuando tengas sed, ve a beber de los cántaros de agua que los muchachos han llenado».

decisions.choice: after them: after the young women
decisions.reason: The pronoun is feminine: Ruth is to follow the young women of verse 8, who come behind the reapers binding the sheaves.

decisions.choice: touch: harm or harass
decisions.reason: To "touch" someone can mean to strike, harm or molest them (Genesis 26:11, 29). A foreign woman alone in the fields could be mistreated; Naomi sees the same danger in verse 22.

decisions.choice: the young men draw water for her
decisions.reason: Water was usually drawn by women (Genesis 24:11), and a foreign gleaner might expect to serve others. Here the men of Boaz's household draw it and she drinks freely.

decisions.choice: I have ordered (Balanced); I have told (Readable)
decisions.reason: The question "have I not commanded ...?" expects the answer yes, so Balanced and Readable state it plainly; Literal keeps the question.

decisions.choice: the women; the water
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who "them" is and what is drawn.

records.literal_gloss: And she fell on her face and bowed down to [the] ground and said to him, why have I found favor in your eyes, to take notice of me, and I [am] a foreigner?

en.L: And she fell on her face and bowed down to the ground and said to him, "Why have I found favor in your eyes, that you take notice of me, when I [am] a foreigner?"
en.B: Ruth fell face down and bowed to the ground. She said to him, "Why have I found such favor with you, that you would take notice of me, when I am a foreigner?"
en.R: Ruth bowed down with her face to the ground. She said to him, "Why are you so kind to me? Why do you care about me? I am a foreigner."

sw.L: Naye akaanguka kifudifudi, akainama mpaka chini, akamwambia, "Kwa nini nimepata kibali machoni pako, hata unanijali, nami ni mgeni?"
sw.B: Ruthu alianguka kifudifudi, akainama mpaka chini. Akamwambia, "Kwa nini nimepata kibali kama hiki kwako, hata unanijali, nami ni mgeni?"
sw.R: Ruthu aliinama mpaka uso wake ukagusa chini. Alimwambia, "Kwa nini unanitendea wema namna hii? Kwa nini unanijali? Mimi ni mgeni."

es.L: Y ella cayó sobre su rostro y se inclinó a tierra y le dijo: «¿Por qué he hallado gracia a tus ojos, para que te fijes en mí, siendo yo extranjera?».
es.B: Rut se postró rostro en tierra y le dijo: «¿Por qué me miras con tanto favor, que te fijas en mí, siendo yo una extranjera?».
es.R: Rut se inclinó con el rostro en tierra. Le dijo: «¿Por qué eres tan bueno conmigo? ¿Por qué te preocupas por mí? Yo soy extranjera».

decisions.choice: take notice of me ... a foreigner: a play on words
decisions.reason: "Take notice of" (hakkir) and "foreigner" (nokhriyyah) sound alike in Hebrew. A foreigner was someone others did not recognize or care about, yet Boaz has recognized her.

decisions.choice: foreigner: one from another people
decisions.reason: Nokhriyyah is a foreign woman, an outsider with no place in Israel by birth, a stronger word than the ger who has settled among the people. Ruth expects nothing as a Moabite (Deuteronomy 23:4).

decisions.choice: fell on her face and bowed: deep respect and thanks
decisions.reason: Bowing to the ground was the way to honor a superior and thank him (1 Samuel 25:23).

decisions.choice: two questions and a statement
decisions.reason: Readable divides the long question into short ones; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: "mgeni" for the foreigner (nokhri)
decisions.reason: Swahili "mgeni" is the ordinary word for someone from elsewhere; the Hebrew play between "take notice of" and "foreigner" (m1) cannot be kept, and the meaning decision explains it.

decisions.choice: "te fijes en mí" ... "extranjera"; the play on words is not kept
decisions.reason: In Hebrew "take notice of" and "foreigner" are built from the same letters (m1). Spanish cannot keep both meanings and the sound; it keeps the meanings, and the meaning decision tells the reader of the play.

records.literal_gloss: And answered Boaz and said to her, told, it has been told to me all that you have done with your mother-in-law after [the] death of your husband, and you left your father and your mother and [the] land of your birth and you came to a people that you did not know yesterday three days ago.

en.L: And Boaz answered and said to her, "It has been fully told to me, all that you have done for your mother-in-law after the death of your husband, and [how] you left your father and your mother and the land of your birth, and came to a people whom you did not know yesterday [or] the day before.
en.B: Boaz answered her, "I have heard the whole story of what you have done for your mother-in-law after your husband's death: how you left your father and mother and the land where you were born, and came to a people you had never known before.
en.R: Boaz answered, "People have told me how good you have been to your mother-in-law since your husband died. You left your father and mother and the country where you were born. You came to live among people you did not know before.

sw.L: Naye Boazi akajibu, akamwambia, "Nimeambiwa kikamilifu yote uliyomtendea mama mkwe wako baada ya kifo cha mumeo, na [jinsi] ulivyomwacha baba yako na mama yako na nchi ya kuzaliwa kwako, ukaja kwa watu usiowajua jana [wala] juzi.

sw.R: Boazi alijibu, "Watu wameniambia jinsi ulivyokuwa mwema kwa mama mkwe wako tangu mumeo alipokufa. Ulimwacha baba yako na mama yako na nchi uliyozaliwa. Ulikuja kuishi kati ya watu usiowajua kabla.

es.L: Y Booz respondió y le dijo: «Se me ha contado bien todo lo que has hecho con tu suegra después de la muerte de tu marido, y [cómo] dejaste a tu padre y a tu madre y la tierra de tu nacimiento, y viniste a un pueblo que no conocías ni ayer ni anteayer.
es.B: Booz le respondió: «Me han contado todo lo que has hecho por tu suegra desde que murió tu marido: cómo dejaste a tu padre y a tu madre y la tierra donde naciste, y viniste a un pueblo que antes no conocías.
es.R: Booz le contestó: «Me han contado lo buena que has sido con tu suegra desde que murió tu esposo. Dejaste a tu padre y a tu madre y el país donde naciste. Viniste a vivir entre gente que antes no conocías.

decisions.choice: it has been fully told: the verb doubled
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the verb for emphasis: Boaz has heard the whole story, and in detail.

decisions.choice: left father, mother and the land of her birth
decisions.reason: The words recall God's call to Abraham to leave his land, his kindred and his father's house (Genesis 12:1). Ruth has made the same kind of break, with no promise given to her.

decisions.choice: yesterday, three days ago: before, in the past
decisions.reason: The pair of time words is a fixed way of saying "previously" (Genesis 31:2). She came to a people who had been strangers to her.

decisions.choice: never known before (Balanced); did not know before (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the time idiom; Literal keeps "yesterday [or] the day before".

decisions.choice: under whose wings: in God's protecting care
decisions.reason: The picture is of a bird sheltering its young under its wings (Deuteronomy 32:11; Psalm 17:8; 36:8; 91:4). The word for wing, kanaf, also means the corner of a garment, and it comes back in 3:9, where Ruth asks Boaz to spread his "wing" over her. The man who prays for her shelter becomes the one through whom it comes.

decisions.choice: wages: the pay due to a worker
decisions.reason: Maskoret is a worker's wage (Genesis 29:15; 31:7), a fitting word in a harvest field. "Repay" and "complete" also come from one root (shalem): Boaz prays that God will pay her in full.

decisions.choice: take refuge: trust oneself to God for protection
decisions.reason: To take refuge in God is to rely on him for safety (Psalm 2:12; 5:12). By coming with Naomi and taking her God as her own (1:16), Ruth has put herself under the care of the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: order of the clauses
decisions.reason: Readable says first that Ruth has come to the LORD for safety, then gives the wish for her reward, in shorter sentences.

decisions.choice: "bajo cuyas alas" at every level
decisions.reason: The picture of God's wings (m1) is kept at every level, as in the English, because Ruth 3:9 picks it up again when Ruth asks Boaz to spread his "ala" over her.

en.L: And she said, "May I find favor in your eyes, my lord, for you have comforted me and spoken to the heart of your maidservant, though I am not like one of your maidservants."
en.B: She said, "May I go on finding favor in your eyes, my lord. You have comforted me and spoken kindly to your servant, though I am not even one of your servant women."
en.R: Ruth said, "Sir, I hope you will always be this kind to me. You have comforted me. You have spoken kindly to me, and I am not even one of your servants."

sw.B: Akasema, "Niendelee kupata kibali machoni pako, bwana wangu. Umenifariji na kusema kwa upole na mtumishi wako, ingawa mimi si hata mmoja wa wajakazi wako."
sw.R: Ruthu alisema, "Bwana, natumaini utaendelea kunitendea wema namna hii. Umenifariji. Umesema nami kwa upole, nami si hata mmoja wa watumishi wako."

es.L: Y ella dijo: «Halle yo gracia a tus ojos, señor mío, porque me has consolado y has hablado al corazón de tu sierva, aunque yo no soy como una de tus siervas».
es.B: Ella dijo: «Que siga yo hallando favor a tus ojos, señor mío. Me has consolado y le has hablado con bondad a tu sierva, aunque ni siquiera soy una de tus siervas».
es.R: Rut le dijo: «Señor, espero que siempre seas así de bueno conmigo. Me has consolado. Me has hablado con bondad, aunque ni siquiera soy una de tus sirvientas».

decisions.choice: may I find favor: a wish, or thanks
alternatives: I have found favor in your eyes
decisions.reason: The verb can be read as a wish ("may I find favor", that is, may your kindness continue) or as a grateful statement ("I am finding favor with you"). Either way she is thanking him.

decisions.choice: spoken to the heart: spoken kindly, reassured
decisions.reason: To speak to someone's heart is to speak words of comfort and encouragement (Genesis 50:21; Isaiah 40:2).

decisions.choice: maidservant: shifchah, a female servant of low rank
decisions.reason: Shifchah is a servant girl, one of the household's workers. Ruth calls herself his shifchah out of humility, yet says she does not even rank with his servant women. In 3:9 she calls herself his 'amah, a servant woman who could become a wife.

decisions.choice: servant, servant women (Balanced); servants (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "maidservant"; Balanced and Readable use the plain word.

decisions.choice: Sir
decisions.reason: "My lord" is a polite address to a man of higher rank, not a title for God; Readable says "Sir".

records.literal_gloss: And said to her Boaz at [the] time of the meal, come near here and eat from the bread and dip your morsel in the vinegar. And she sat at [the] side of the harvesters, and he held out to her roasted grain, and she ate and was satisfied and had left over.

en.L: And Boaz said to her at the time of the meal, "Come near here and eat some of the bread, and dip your piece in the vinegar." So she sat beside the harvesters, and he held out roasted grain to her, and she ate and was satisfied and had some left over.
en.B: When mealtime came, Boaz said to her, "Come over here and help yourself to some bread. Dip your piece in the sour wine." So she sat down beside the harvesters, and he passed her some roasted grain. She ate all she wanted and still had some left over.
en.R: When it was time to eat, Boaz said to Ruth, "Come here and eat some bread. Dip it in the sour wine." So Ruth sat down with the harvesters, and Boaz handed her some roasted grain. She ate until she was full, and there was still some left over.

sw.L: Naye Boazi akamwambia wakati wa kula, "Karibia hapa, ule mkate, na uchovye kipande chako katika siki." Basi akaketi kando ya wavunaji, naye akampa bisi, naye akala, akashiba, akabakiza.
sw.B: Wakati wa chakula ulipofika, Boazi alimwambia, "Njoo hapa ujipatie mkate. Chovya kipande chako katika divai chachu." Basi aliketi kando ya wavunaji, naye akampa bisi. Alikula akashiba, na bado akabakiza.
sw.R: Wakati wa kula ulipofika, Boazi alimwambia Ruthu, "Njoo hapa ule mkate. Uchovye katika divai chachu." Kwa hiyo Ruthu aliketi pamoja na wavunaji, naye Boazi akampa bisi. Alikula mpaka akashiba, na bado vikabaki vingine.

es.L: Y Booz le dijo a la hora de la comida: «Acércate aquí y come del pan, y moja tu bocado en el vinagre». Y ella se sentó junto a los segadores, y él le ofreció grano tostado, y ella comió y se sació y le sobró.
es.B: Cuando llegó la hora de comer, Booz le dijo: «Ven aquí y sírvete pan. Moja tu bocado en el vino agrio». Así que ella se sentó junto a los segadores, y él le pasó grano tostado. Comió todo lo que quiso, y todavía le sobró.
es.R: Cuando llegó la hora de comer, Booz le dijo a Rut: «Ven aquí a comer pan. Mójalo en el vino agrio». Rut se sentó con los segadores, y Booz le dio grano tostado. Ella comió hasta quedar satisfecha, y todavía le sobró.

decisions.choice: vinegar: a sour wine drink or dip
decisions.reason: Chomets is wine gone sour (Numbers 6:3). Workers dipped bread in it; it was a cheap, refreshing part of a field meal.

decisions.choice: roasted grain: heads of grain parched over a fire
decisions.reason: Fresh ears roasted over a fire were common food at harvest time and on a journey (Leviticus 23:14; 1 Samuel 17:17).

decisions.choice: ate and was satisfied and had left over: plenty after emptiness
decisions.reason: Naomi came home "empty" (1:21). Now Ruth eats her fill and has food to spare, which she takes home to Naomi (verse 18).

decisions.choice: sour wine
decisions.reason: "Vinegar" suggests a kitchen liquid to most readers; Balanced and Readable say what it was. Literal keeps "vinegar".

source.text: וַתָּ֖קָם לְלַקֵּ֑ט וַיְצַו֩ בֹּ֨עַז אֶת־נְעָרָ֜יו לֵאמֹ֗ר גַּ֣ם בֵּ֧ין הָֽעֳמָרִ֛ים תְּלַקֵּ֖ט וְלֹ֥א תַכְלִימֽוּהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And she rose to glean, and commanded Boaz his young men, saying, even between the sheaves let her glean, and do not humiliate her.

en.L: And she rose to glean, and Boaz commanded his young men, saying, "Let her glean even among the sheaves, and do not put her to shame.
en.B: When she got up to glean, Boaz gave orders to his young men: "Let her glean even among the sheaves, and do not embarrass her.
en.R: When Ruth got up to go back to work, Boaz gave orders to his young men. He said, "Let her pick up grain even where the bundles are lying. Do not make her feel ashamed.

sw.L: Naye akainuka ili aokote masazo, naye Boazi akawaamuru vijana wake, akisema, "Na aokote hata kati ya miganda, wala msimtie aibu.
sw.B: Alipoinuka kwenda kuokota masazo, Boazi aliwaagiza vijana wake: "Mwacheni aokote hata kati ya miganda, wala msimwaibishe.
sw.R: Ruthu alipoinuka kurudi kazini, Boazi aliwaagiza vijana wake. Alisema, "Mwacheni aokote nafaka hata mahali ambapo mafungu yamelala. Msimfanye aone aibu.

es.L: Y ella se levantó para recoger espigas, y Booz mandó a sus criados, diciendo: «Que recoja espigas aun entre las gavillas, y no la {{plural_you:avergüencen|avergoncéis}}.
es.B: Cuando ella se levantó para recoger espigas, Booz dio órdenes a sus criados: «{{plural_you:Déjenla|Dejadla}} recoger espigas aun entre las gavillas, y no la {{plural_you:avergüencen|avergoncéis}}.
es.R: Cuando Rut se levantó para volver al trabajo, Booz dio órdenes a sus muchachos. Les dijo: «{{plural_you:Déjenla|Dejadla}} recoger grano aun donde están los manojos. No la {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} sentir avergonzada.

decisions.choice: even among the sheaves: beyond the usual right
decisions.reason: Boaz grants what Ruth asked for (verse 7). Gleaners normally worked only where the reapers had already cleared the field; among the sheaves they could be suspected of taking the owner's grain.

decisions.choice: do not put her to shame: do not insult or humiliate her
decisions.reason: The verb means to shame or humiliate someone, by words or by treatment (1 Samuel 25:7, 15). No one is to treat her as a thief or an intruder.

decisions.choice: to go back to work
decisions.reason: Readable says that she went back to gleaning after the meal.

source.text: וְגַ֛ם שֹׁל־תָּשֹׁ֥לּוּ לָ֖הּ מִן־הַצְּבָתִ֑ים וַעֲזַבְתֶּ֥ם וְלִקְּטָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א תִגְעֲרוּ־בָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And also pull, pull out for her from the bundles and leave [them], and she will glean, and do not rebuke her.

en.L: And also be sure to pull out [some] for her from the bundles and leave [them], and let her glean [them], and do not rebuke her."
en.B: And even pull out some stalks from the bundles for her and leave them for her to glean. Do not scold her."
en.R: Also pull out some stalks from the bundles on purpose and leave them for her to pick up. Do not speak harshly to her."

sw.L: Na pia hakika mvute [masuke] kutoka kwenye mafungu kwa ajili yake, myaache, ili ayaokote, wala msimkemee."
sw.B: Na hata mvute masuke kadhaa kutoka kwenye mafungu kwa ajili yake, myaache ili ayaokote. Msimkaripie."
sw.R: Pia mvute masuke kadhaa kutoka kwenye mafungu kwa makusudi, myaache ili ayaokote. Msiseme naye kwa ukali."

es.L: Y también {{plural_you:saquen|sacad}} bien para ella de los manojos y {{plural_you:déjenlos|dejadlos}}, y que [los] recoja, y no la {{plural_you:reprendan|reprendáis}}».
es.B: Y hasta {{plural_you:saquen|sacad}} para ella algunas espigas de los manojos y {{plural_you:déjenlas|dejadlas}} para que las recoja. No la {{plural_you:regañen|regañéis}}».
es.R: Además, {{plural_you:saquen|sacad}} a propósito algunas espigas de los manojos y {{plural_you:déjenlas|dejadlas}} para que ella las recoja. No le {{plural_you:hablen|habléis}} con dureza».

decisions.choice: pull, pull out: on purpose
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis: the reapers are to pull stalks out deliberately and drop them for her.

decisions.choice: bundles: handfuls of cut stalks
decisions.reason: Tsevatim, found only here, are the handfuls a reaper gathers before they are tied into sheaves.

decisions.choice: leave them: generosity beyond the law
decisions.reason: The law said a forgotten sheaf was to be left for the poor (Deuteronomy 24:19). Boaz tells his men to leave grain for Ruth on purpose, going beyond what the law required.

decisions.choice: on purpose
decisions.reason: Readable expresses the doubled verb with "on purpose"; Balanced uses "even", Literal "be sure to".

source.text: וַתְּלַקֵּ֥ט בַּשָּׂדֶ֖ה עַד־הָעָ֑רֶב וַתַּחְבֹּט֙ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־לִקֵּ֔טָה וַיְהִ֖י כְּאֵיפָ֥ה שְׂעֹרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And she gleaned in the field until the evening, and she beat out what she had gleaned, and it was about an ephah [of] barley.

en.L: So she gleaned in the field until evening, and she beat out what she had gleaned, and it was about an ephah of barley.
en.B: So Ruth gleaned in the field until evening. Then she beat out what she had gleaned, and it came to {{units:about 20 quarts|about an ephah}} of barley.
en.R: Ruth kept picking up grain in the field until evening. Then she beat the stalks to knock the grain loose. She had {{units:about 20 quarts|about an ephah}} of barley.

sw.L: Basi akaokota masazo shambani mpaka jioni, akapiga alichokiokota, nacho kikawa yapata efa moja ya shayiri.
sw.B: Basi Ruthu aliokota masazo shambani mpaka jioni. Kisha alipiga alichokiokota, nacho kikawa {{units:karibu lita 22|karibu efa moja}} za shayiri.
sw.R: Ruthu aliendelea kuokota nafaka shambani mpaka jioni. Kisha aliyapiga masuke ili nafaka itoke. Alikuwa na {{units:karibu lita 22|karibu efa moja}} za shayiri.

es.L: Y recogió espigas en el campo hasta la tarde, y desgranó lo que había recogido, y fue como un efa de cebada.
es.B: Así que Rut recogió espigas en el campo hasta la tarde. Luego desgranó lo que había recogido, y salieron {{units:unos 22 litros|como un efa}} de cebada.
es.R: Rut siguió recogiendo grano en el campo hasta la tarde. Después golpeó las espigas para soltar el grano. Tenía {{units:unos 22 litros|como un efa}} de cebada.

decisions.choice: beat out: threshing by hand
decisions.reason: A small amount of grain was threshed by beating the stalks with a stick so that the kernels fell free (Judges 6:11). Ruth carries home grain, not bundles of stalks.

decisions.choice: about an ephah of barley: a very large day's gleaning
decisions.reason: An ephah was a dry measure of about 20 quarts. It is far more than a gleaner could expect from one day, enough to feed two women for many days, and it shows how much Boaz's orders (verses 15-16) helped her.

decisions.choice: about 20 quarts, with the ephah as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the modern measure, with the ephah as the alternative; Literal keeps the ephah.

decisions.choice: beat the stalks to knock the grain loose
decisions.reason: Readable explains what beating out the grain means.

decisions.choice: "karibu lita 22" (about 22 litres) for the ephah, with "karibu efa moja" as the reader setting
alternatives: US quarts as in the English
decisions.reason: Metric by default, as the Swahili style guide sets, at the ephah value of 22 litres the Pentateuch drafts use; Literal keeps "efa".

decisions.choice: "unos 22 litros" by default, "como un efa" with the measures setting
decisions.reason: As the Pentateuch terms set for Spanish: an ephah is about 22 litres, given in metric by default with the original measure as the alternative; Literal keeps "efa".

source.text: וַתִּשָּׂא֙ וַתָּב֣וֹא הָעִ֔יר וַתֵּ֥רֶא חֲמוֹתָ֖הּ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־לִקֵּ֑טָה וַתּוֹצֵא֙ וַתִּתֶּן־לָ֔הּ אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־הוֹתִ֖רָה מִשָּׂבְעָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And she lifted [it] and came [into] the city, and saw her mother-in-law what she had gleaned; and she brought out and gave to her what she had left over from her being satisfied.

en.L: And she picked [it] up and went into the town, and her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned; and she brought out and gave her what she had left over after she was satisfied.
en.B: She picked it up and went into the town, and her mother-in-law saw how much she had gleaned. Ruth also brought out what she had left over after eating her fill, and gave it to her.
en.R: Ruth carried it back into town, and her mother-in-law saw how much grain she had gathered. Then Ruth took out the food left over from her meal and gave it to Naomi.

sw.L: Naye akakiinua, akaingia mjini, naye mama mkwe wake akaona alichokiokota; naye akatoa, akampa alichobakiza baada ya kushiba.
sw.B: Alikibeba, akaingia mjini, na mama mkwe wake akaona kiasi alichokiokota. Ruthu pia alitoa chakula alichobakiza baada ya kula akashiba, akampa.
sw.R: Ruthu aliibeba mpaka mjini, na mama mkwe wake akaona wingi wa nafaka aliyoikusanya. Kisha Ruthu alitoa chakula kilichobaki baada ya kula, akampa Naomi.

es.L: Y [lo] alzó y entró en la ciudad, y su suegra vio lo que había recogido; y sacó y le dio lo que le había sobrado después de saciarse.
es.B: Lo cargó y entró en el pueblo, y su suegra vio cuánto había recogido. Rut sacó también lo que le había sobrado después de comer hasta saciarse, y se lo dio.
es.R: Rut lo llevó al pueblo, y su suegra vio cuánto grano había juntado. Entonces Rut sacó la comida que le había sobrado y se la dio a Noemí.

decisions.choice: her mother-in-law saw
decisions.reason: The Hebrew as vowelled reads "her mother-in-law saw". The same letters could be read "she showed her mother-in-law", and some ancient translations have that. The scene is the same either way.

decisions.choice: what she had left over: the food from her meal
decisions.reason: This is the roasted grain left over at the midday meal (verse 14), which Ruth has kept for Naomi.

decisions.choice: how much she had gleaned
decisions.reason: "How much" makes clear what struck Naomi, the size of the gleaning (verse 17).

source.text: וַתֹּאמֶר֩ לָ֨הּ חֲמוֹתָ֜הּ אֵיפֹ֨ה לִקַּ֤טְתְּ הַיּוֹם֙ וְאָ֣נָה עָשִׂ֔ית יְהִ֥י מַכִּירֵ֖ךְ בָּר֑וּךְ וַתַּגֵּ֣ד לַחֲמוֹתָ֗הּ אֵ֤ת אֲשֶׁר־עָשְׂתָה֙ עִמּ֔וֹ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר שֵׁ֤ם הָאִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשִׂ֧יתִי עִמּ֛וֹ הַיּ֖וֹם בֹּֽעַז׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to her her mother-in-law, where did you glean today, and where did you work? May be the [one] taking notice of you blessed. And she told her mother-in-law [with] whom she had worked and said, [the] name of the man whom I worked with him today [is] Boaz.

en.L: And her mother-in-law said to her, "Where did you glean today, and where did you work? May the one who took notice of you be blessed!" And she told her mother-in-law with whom she had worked, and said, "The name of the man with whom I worked today [is] Boaz."
en.B: Her mother-in-law asked her, "Where did you glean today? Where did you work? Blessed be the man who took notice of you!" So Ruth told her mother-in-law about the man she had worked with. "The man I worked with today is named Boaz," she said.
en.R: Naomi asked her, "Where did you pick up all this grain today? Where did you work? Bless the man who was so kind to you!" Ruth told her mother-in-law whose field she had worked in. She said, "The man whose field I worked in today is named Boaz."

sw.L: Naye mama mkwe wake akamwambia, "Umeokota masazo wapi leo, na umefanya kazi wapi? Na abarikiwe yule aliyekujali!" Naye akamweleza mama mkwe wake ni kwa nani alikofanya kazi, akasema, "Jina la mtu ambaye nimefanya kazi kwake leo [ni] Boazi."
sw.B: Mama mkwe wake alimwuliza, "Umeokota masazo wapi leo? Umefanya kazi wapi? Abarikiwe mtu aliyekujali!" Basi Ruthu alimweleza mama mkwe wake habari za mtu aliyefanya kazi kwake. Akasema, "Mtu niliyefanya kazi kwake leo anaitwa Boazi."
sw.R: Naomi alimwuliza, "Umeokota nafaka hii yote wapi leo? Ulifanya kazi wapi? Na abarikiwe mtu aliyekutendea wema hivi!" Ruthu alimweleza mama mkwe wake ni shamba la nani alimofanya kazi. Alisema, "Mtu ambaye nimefanya kazi shambani mwake leo anaitwa Boazi."

es.L: Y su suegra le dijo: «¿Dónde recogiste espigas hoy, y dónde trabajaste? Bendito sea el que se fijó en ti». Y ella contó a su suegra con quién había trabajado, y dijo: «El nombre del hombre con quien trabajé hoy [es] Booz».
es.B: Su suegra le preguntó: «¿Dónde recogiste espigas hoy? ¿Dónde trabajaste? ¡Bendito sea el hombre que se fijó en ti!». Entonces Rut le contó a su suegra con quién había trabajado. «El hombre con quien trabajé hoy se llama Booz», le dijo.
es.R: Noemí le preguntó: «¿Dónde recogiste todo este grano hoy? ¿Dónde trabajaste? ¡Bendito sea el hombre que fue tan bueno contigo!». Rut le contó a su suegra en qué campo había trabajado. Le dijo: «El hombre en cuyo campo trabajé hoy se llama Booz».

decisions.choice: may the one who took notice of you be blessed: Naomi sees a generous patron
decisions.reason: So much grain and food could only come from someone's special kindness. Naomi blesses him before she knows who he is. "Took notice of" is the word Ruth used in verse 10.

decisions.choice: Boaz: the name held to the end
decisions.reason: Ruth's answer puts the name last, so that it lands with weight, and Naomi reacts to it at once (verse 20).

decisions.choice: whose field she had worked in
decisions.reason: To work "with" a man here means to work on his land; Readable says so. Literal and Balanced keep "worked with".

decisions.choice: all this grain
decisions.reason: Readable adds what prompted the question, the amount she brought home.

source.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר נָעֳמִ֜י לְכַלָּתָ֗הּ בָּר֥וּךְ הוּא֙ לַיהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר֙ לֹא־עָזַ֣ב חַסְדּ֔וֹ אֶת־הַחַיִּ֖ים וְאֶת־הַמֵּתִ֑ים וַתֹּ֧אמֶר לָ֣הּ נָעֳמִ֗י קָר֥וֹב לָ֨נוּ֙ הָאִ֔ישׁ מִֽגֹּאֲלֵ֖נוּ הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Naomi to her daughter-in-law, blessed [is] he by Yahweh, who has not forsaken his steadfast love with the living and with the dead. And said to her Naomi, near to us [is] the man; one of our redeemers [is] he.

en.L: And Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, "Blessed [is] he by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who has not forsaken {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} steadfast love to the living and to the dead!" And Naomi said to her, "The man [is] near to us; he [is] one of our redeemers."
en.B: Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless him! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has not stopped showing {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful love to the living and to the dead." Naomi went on, "That man is a close relative of ours. He is one of our family redeemers."
en.R: Naomi said to Ruth, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless him! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has kept on showing {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful love to those of us who are alive and to those who have died." Naomi also said, "That man is a close relative of ours. He is one of our family redeemers, who have a duty to help us."

sw.L: Naye Naomi akamwambia mkwe wake, "Na abarikiwe na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ambaye hakuuacha upendo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} usiokoma kwa walio hai na kwa wafu!" Naye Naomi akamwambia, "Mtu huyo [ni] wa karibu nasi; yeye [ni] mmoja wa wakombozi wetu."
sw.B: Naomi alimwambia mkwe wake, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ambariki! {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hajaacha kuwaonyesha walio hai na waliokufa upendo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} usiokoma." Naomi akaendelea, "Mtu huyo ni jamaa yetu wa karibu. Yeye ni mmoja wa wakombozi wa jamaa yetu."
sw.R: Naomi alimwambia Ruthu, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ambariki! {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameendelea kuonyesha upendo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} usiokoma kwetu sisi tulio hai na kwa wale waliokufa." Naomi pia alisema, "Mtu huyo ni jamaa yetu wa karibu. Yeye ni mmoja wa wakombozi wa jamaa yetu, walio na wajibu wa kutusaidia."

es.L: Y Noemí dijo a su nuera: «Bendito [sea] él {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, que no ha abandonado {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} amor leal para con los vivos y para con los muertos». Y le dijo Noemí: «El hombre [es] cercano a nosotras; él [es] uno de nuestros redentores».
es.B: Noemí le dijo a su nuera: «¡Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo bendiga! {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no ha dejado de mostrar {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} amor fiel a los vivos y a los muertos». Y añadió Noemí: «Ese hombre es pariente cercano nuestro. Es uno de nuestros parientes redentores».
es.R: Noemí le dijo a Rut: «¡Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo bendiga! {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha seguido mostrando {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} amor fiel a los que estamos vivos y a los que han muerto». Noemí también le dijo: «Ese hombre es pariente cercano nuestro. Es uno de nuestros parientes redentores, que tienen el deber de ayudarnos».

decisions.choice: who has not forsaken: the LORD, rather than Boaz
alternatives: Boaz, who has not stopped showing kindness to the living and the dead
decisions.reason: "Who" could refer to the LORD or to Boaz. The same words are used of the LORD in Genesis 24:27, and Naomi had prayed that the LORD would show such love (1:8), so the LORD is the likelier subject: Naomi, who said the LORD had turned against her (1:20-21), now sees his care. If it refers to Boaz, Naomi is praising his kindness to the family.

decisions.choice: steadfast love to the living and to the dead
decisions.reason: Chesed is loyal, faithful love that keeps faith within a bond and goes beyond what duty requires. The living are Naomi and Ruth; the dead are Elimelech and his sons, whose family line and land are not forgotten (1:8; 4:5, 10).

decisions.choice: redeemer (go'el): the relative bound to help
decisions.reason: A go'el was a close relative with the duty to stand up for a family in trouble: to buy back land a relative had to sell (Leviticus 25:25), to buy back a relative sold into slavery (Leviticus 25:47-49), and to keep a dead man's name and line alive, as the related law of the brother-in-law requires (Deuteronomy 25:5-10). Naomi sees hope for her family's land and line in Boaz; chapters 3-4 show how.

decisions.choice: near to us: a close relative
decisions.reason: "Near" here means close by kinship. Naomi's words also hint that there may be others nearer (3:12).

decisions.choice: steadfast love (Literal); faithful love (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 34:6, Deuteronomy and Joshua 2:12, so that the loyalty in the word is kept; "kindness" alone would leave it out.

decisions.choice: redeemer (Literal); family redeemer (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "Redeemer" alone may suggest only a religious sense to modern readers; "family redeemer" shows that he acts for his relatives.

decisions.choice: who have a duty to help us
decisions.reason: Readable says briefly what a family redeemer was for.

decisions.choice: "mkombozi" (redeemer) at Literal; "mkombozi wa jamaa" (family redeemer) at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As agreed for Ruth in every language. "Mkombozi" alone could be heard as the Redeemer of Christian speech; "wa jamaa" ties the word to the family duty the meaning decision explains (m3).

decisions.choice: "redentor" (L); "pariente redentor" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets for the Hebrew go'el, the relative bound to buy back family land and care for the family line (m3): Literal says "redentor", and Balanced and Readable "pariente redentor", so that a reader does not think only of the Redeemer of later Scripture.

source.text: וַתֹּ֖אמֶר ר֣וּת הַמּוֹאֲבִיָּ֑ה גַּ֣ם׀כִּי־אָמַ֣ר אֵלַ֗י עִם־הַנְּעָרִ֤ים אֲשֶׁר־לִי֙ תִּדְבָּקִ֔ין עַ֣ד אִם־כִּלּ֔וּ אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַקָּצִ֖יר אֲשֶׁר־לִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Ruth the Moabite, also that he said to me, with the young men who [belong] to me you will stay close until they have finished all the harvest which [belongs] to me.

en.L: And Ruth the Moabite said, "He even said to me, 'Keep close to the young men who [are] mine until they have finished all the harvest that [is] mine.'"
en.B: Then Ruth the Moabite said, "He even told me, 'Stay close to my workers until they have finished all my harvest.'"
en.R: Ruth, the woman from Moab, said, "He also told me, 'Stay with my workers until they have brought in all my harvest.'"

sw.L: Naye Ruthu Mmoabu akasema, "Tena aliniambia, 'Kaa karibu na vijana walio wangu mpaka watakapomaliza mavuno yote yaliyo yangu.'"
sw.B: Kisha Ruthu Mmoabu alisema, "Hata aliniambia, 'Kaa karibu na wafanyakazi wangu mpaka watakapomaliza mavuno yangu yote.'"
sw.R: Ruthu, yule mwanamke wa Moabu, alisema, "Pia aliniambia, 'Kaa pamoja na wafanyakazi wangu mpaka watakapomaliza kuvuna mavuno yangu yote.'"

es.L: Y Rut la moabita dijo: «Además me dijo: “Quédate junto a los criados que [son] míos hasta que hayan acabado toda la siega que [es] mía”».
es.B: Entonces Rut la moabita dijo: «Además me dijo: “Quédate junto a mis trabajadores hasta que terminen toda mi cosecha”».
es.R: Rut, la mujer de Moab, dijo: «También me dijo: “Quédate con mis trabajadores hasta que hayan recogido toda mi cosecha”».

decisions.choice: the young men: the whole harvest crew
decisions.reason: Boaz had told her to keep close to his young women (verse 8); Ruth reports it with the masculine word, which can cover the whole group of workers. Naomi answers with the young women (verse 22).

decisions.choice: keep close: the same verb as in verse 8
decisions.reason: Dabaq, "cling, keep close", runs through the book (1:14; 2:8, 23).

decisions.choice: my workers
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a word that includes men and women; Literal keeps "young men", so the change from verse 8 can be seen.

source.text: וַתֹּ֥אמֶר נָעֳמִ֖י אֶל־ר֣וּת כַּלָּתָ֑הּ ט֣וֹב בִּתִּ֗י כִּ֤י תֵֽצְאִי֙ עִם־נַ֣עֲרוֹתָ֔יו וְלֹ֥א יִפְגְּעוּ־בָ֖ךְ בְּשָׂדֶ֥ה אַחֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Naomi to Ruth her daughter-in-law, good, my daughter, that you go out with his young women, and they will not meet you in another field.

en.L: And Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, "[It is] good, my daughter, that you go out with his young women, so that they do not fall upon you in another field."
en.B: Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, "It is best, my daughter, that you go out with his young women. In someone else's field you might be harmed."
en.R: Naomi said to Ruth, "My daughter, it is good for you to go out with the young women who work for Boaz. In another field someone might hurt you."

sw.L: Naye Naomi akamwambia Ruthu mkwe wake, "[Ni] vema, binti yangu, utoke pamoja na wasichana wake, wasije wakakushambulia katika shamba lingine."
sw.B: Naomi alimwambia Ruthu mkwe wake, "Ni bora, binti yangu, utoke pamoja na wasichana wake. Katika shamba la mtu mwingine ungeweza kudhuriwa."
sw.R: Naomi alimwambia Ruthu, "Binti yangu, ni vizuri utoke pamoja na wasichana wanaomfanyia Boazi kazi. Katika shamba lingine mtu angeweza kukuumiza."

es.L: Y Noemí dijo a Rut su nuera: «[Es] bueno, hija mía, que salgas con sus criadas, para que no te maltraten en otro campo».
es.B: Noemí le dijo a Rut, su nuera: «Lo mejor, hija mía, es que salgas con sus criadas. En el campo de otro podrían hacerte daño».
es.R: Noemí le dijo a Rut: «Hija mía, es bueno que salgas con las muchachas que trabajan para Booz. En otro campo alguien podría hacerte daño».

decisions.choice: fall upon you: attack or harm you
decisions.reason: The verb paga' means to meet, and often to meet with hostile intent, to attack (Judges 8:21; 15:12). Naomi fears what could happen to a young foreign woman alone among strangers.

decisions.choice: with his young women
decisions.reason: Naomi takes up Boaz's own instruction (verse 8) rather than Ruth's wording in verse 21: she is safest among the women.

decisions.choice: you might be harmed (Balanced); someone might hurt you (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "they" means people in general; Balanced and Readable say it without naming who.

source.text: וַתִּדְבַּ֞ק בְּנַעֲר֥וֹת בֹּ֨עַז֙ לְלַקֵּ֔ט עַד־כְּל֥וֹת קְצִֽיר־הַשְּׂעֹרִ֖ים וּקְצִ֣יר הַֽחִטִּ֑ים וַתֵּ֖שֶׁב אֶת־חֲמוֹתָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And she stayed close to [the] young women of Boaz to glean until [the] end of [the] harvest of the barley and [the] harvest of the wheat; and she dwelt with her mother-in-law.

en.L: So she kept close to the young women of Boaz to glean until the end of the barley harvest and the wheat harvest; and she lived with her mother-in-law.
en.B: So Ruth stayed close to Boaz's young women and gleaned until the barley and wheat harvests were over. And she went on living with her mother-in-law.
en.R: So Ruth worked beside the young women in Boaz's fields, picking up grain until the barley and wheat harvests were over. All that time she lived with her mother-in-law.

sw.L: Basi akakaa karibu na wasichana wa Boazi ili kuokota masazo mpaka mwisho wa mavuno ya shayiri na mavuno ya ngano; naye akakaa pamoja na mama mkwe wake.
sw.B: Basi Ruthu alikaa karibu na wasichana wa Boazi, akaokota masazo mpaka mavuno ya shayiri na ya ngano yalipokwisha. Naye aliendelea kuishi pamoja na mama mkwe wake.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Ruthu alifanya kazi pamoja na wasichana katika mashamba ya Boazi, akiokota nafaka mpaka mavuno ya shayiri na ya ngano yalipokwisha. Muda wote huo aliishi pamoja na mama mkwe wake.

es.L: Así que se quedó junto a las criadas de Booz para recoger espigas hasta el fin de la siega de la cebada y de la siega del trigo; y habitaba con su suegra.
es.B: Así que Rut se quedó junto a las criadas de Booz y recogió espigas hasta que terminaron la siega de la cebada y la del trigo. Y siguió viviendo con su suegra.
es.R: Así que Rut trabajó junto a las muchachas en los campos de Booz, recogiendo grano hasta que terminaron las cosechas de la cebada y del trigo. Durante todo ese tiempo vivió con su suegra.

decisions.choice: the barley harvest and the wheat harvest: about seven weeks
decisions.reason: Barley ripened first, around Passover, and wheat a few weeks later; the season ran about seven weeks, to the Feast of Weeks (Deuteronomy 16:9-10). Ruth came at its start (1:22).

decisions.choice: she lived with her mother-in-law: the season ends without a next step
decisions.reason: The chapter closes with Ruth still at Naomi's side, as she promised (1:16). Weeks have passed and nothing more has come of the meeting with Boaz, which sets the scene for Naomi's plan in 3:1.

decisions.choice: worked beside the young women in Boaz's fields
decisions.reason: Readable says what keeping close to the young women meant in practice.
